- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.20) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% above recent mean), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.40) and price is trending up, model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% to prevent overconfidence in upward momentum.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 3+ consecutive 0.10–0.20), model tends to lag; add 1–2% lag correction to forecast to account for delayed reaction.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70% of 30-day moving average, model is overconfident; apply 5–10% downward adjustment to avoid “overfitting” to recent highs.
